title: Bermuda bar: a stranger's birthday unlocks a woman's phone
summary: Chris Ramsay tells of Bermuda bar: a stranger's birthday unlocks a woman's phone, about unspecified at a bar in Bermuda, and says they saw it or took part. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: So I said, "Um, put in your birthday." And he puts in his birthday and the phone opens.

plain: A guest named Chris Ramsay tells a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about a night in a bar in Bermuda, at no date he gives. Ramsay says that when someone was trying to get into a woman's locked phone, he told a stranger to type in his own birthday, and the phone opened. He tells it as an example of an uncanny sense of knowing things, the kind of ability he links to the idea that something is pushing human minds forward.
